svg.title: An A/B test with a guardrail: resolution rate lifts but refusal rate breaches
svg.desc: One week of live chatbot traffic split 50/50 between an old prompt (control, n=400) and a new prompt (treatment, n=400). Primary metric, resolution rate: control 168/400 = 0.420, treatment 200/400 = 0.500, an absolute lift of +0.080 (+8.0 pp) and a relative lift of +19.0%. A two-proportion z-test gives pooled rate p = (168+200)/(400+400) = 0.460, standard error SE = 0.03524, z = 2.270, and a two-sided p-value of 0.0232, which is below alpha = 0.05, so the primary lift is statistically significant. Guardrail metric, refusal rate: control 20/400 = 0.050, treatment 40/400 = 0.100, a change of +0.050 (+5.0 pp) against an allowed margin of +2 pp, so the guardrail is breached. Verdict: do not ship, because a significant primary gain is necessary but not sufficient when the guardrail regresses.
